changelog: New in 1.2.0 — Joshua's Detail Editor findings from 2026-10-25, built in full. (1) COLOUR: both viewpoints now show the world in the game's own colours — solid grass-green ground with the grid kept, asphalt road faces, buildings in muted building colours, water in the game's blue; the selected portion stands out in orange and gold. (2) COMPASS bottom-right and SCALE bottom-left, like the Map Editor: the scale reads miles zoomed out and feet zoomed in, both are real screen elements (clicks land on them, not through them), the compass click resets north, and clicking the scale opens a measure — click points and the length is reported. (3) SPEED: panning zoomed into a long road was sluggish because the old drawing rebuilt the road's chain structure the slow way on every frame and drew every point of the whole piece; now only the part in view is drawn and the chain is built once, properly — on a 4,000-point test piece a zoomed-in frame went from about 2,100 ms to about 16 ms. (4) SEGMENTATION DENSITY: roads now open with light segmentation (a handle about every 30 m, just enough to nudge the road); right-click a portion and choose Resegment to make just that portion fine, Coarsen to put it back — the road's own points are never created or destroyed by density. (5) LASSO: with a road open, Shift+drag draws a loop on the grass; the segmented pieces of THE OPEN ROAD ONLY inside it become the working portion, the view zooms to fit it, and the points inside are selected as a group — Delete (the toolbar button or the Delete key) then removes the whole section in ONE operation and ONE undo step: the points, their segments and the face inside go; a middle section leaves the two sides unconnected, an end section shortens the road. Panning never clears a selection. (6) CLICK-SWITCH: clicking another road now works — the current road's edits are saved first (the usual GitHub round trip), then the clicked road opens highlighted as the new working piece. This is also the LAST hand-installed Detail Editor: its launcher is a bootstrap shim — when the suite updater stages a newer payload under ~/.local/share/adamsville-suite/detail-editor/updates/current (with a VERSION file), the editor launches from there instead; anything wrong with the staged copy and the installed one starts, silently.
